summary: A man in his 20s floating the Yampa River near the D-Hole in downtown Steamboat Springs on a double inner tube with a friend became separated from the tube in near-peak spring runoff (~3,110 cfs, more than four times the safe commercial tubing flow); wearing no life jacket, he clung to a tree about 30 feet from shore for 15-20 minutes before bystanders called 911. Steamboat Springs Fire Rescue paramedics reached him with throw bags — Deputy Fire Chief Chuck Cerasoli's second throw bag downriver succeeded — and he was transported to Yampa Valley Medical Center with hypothermic conditions.
location: Yampa River near the D-Hole, downtown Steamboat Springs
notes: Incident Sunday evening 2016-06-05 (Sunday verified, America/Denver); article 'Tuber rescued from raging Yampa River' published Jun 6, 2016 by Scott Franz. Details verified via the run-283 live-browser read of the Pilot article (the Pilot's own search returns only ~77 most-recent results with no pagination, so 2016 content was reached via site: queries + year-archive pages; no paywall/rate-limit hit). Companion on the double tube not counted as a victim. Typing follows id 1613 (stranded tubers: lost/stranded/injury).
